Answer: B
Reason: Comparison of the initial (Figure 1) and follow-up (Figure 7) chest radiographs reveals a marked increase in the number and size of intrapulmonary cavities with new air-fluid levels, indicating disease progression consistent with Mounier-Kuhn Syndrome. Management for this condition focuses on treating recurrent infections with antibiotics and employing physiotherapy to aid secretion clearance due to impaired mucociliary function.
